rules.title: A download is run straight in a shell
rules.description: A shell was started with a command that downloads a script and runs it without saving it first (curl/wget piped to sh). Attackers and some installers do this; nothing is checked before the script runs.

sigma.title: Linux Shell Pipe to Shell / Curl Usage piped to shell
sigma.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)

falsepositives: Official one-line installers (Homebrew, rustup) run on purpose

rules.title: An office app started a shell or script
rules.description: Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Outlook started a command shell or script interpreter. Documents with malicious macros do this; ordinary documents don't.

sigma.title: Suspicious Microsoft Office Child Process - MacOS
sigma.author: Sohan G (D4rkCiph3r)

rules.title: Shell history is being wiped
rules.description: A command clears or disables the shell's history file, which removes the record of what was typed. Intruders do this to cover their tracks.

sigma.title: History File Deletion / Clear Command History
sigma.author: Patrick Bareiss; Ömer Günal

rules.title: The firewall is being switched off or emptied
rules.description: A command turns off the firewall or deletes all of its rules, which opens the computer to the network. Malware and intruders do this before they connect out or listen.

sigma.title: Disable Or Stop Services / Firewall Disabled via Command Line
sigma.author: Qalaa, after SigmaHQ lnx_firewall_disable and macos_disable_security_tools

rules.title: A download's quarantine mark is being removed
rules.description: The command removes the mark macOS puts on downloaded files, so Gatekeeper won't check the program before it runs. Malware installers ask people to do this.

rules.title: A script is showing a fake password prompt
rules.description: AppleScript is displaying a dialog that asks for a password with hidden input. Info-stealers (for example Atomic Stealer) use this to get the login password.

rules.title: A program is being given owner privileges when run
rules.description: chmod sets the setuid or setgid bit, so the program runs with its owner's rights. Attackers use it to keep root access.

rules.title: A program is running from a temporary folder
rules.description: A program started from /tmp, /var/tmp or /dev/shm, folders anyone can write to. Downloaded malware often runs from there.
falsepositives: Build tools and AppImages that unpack into /tmp
